::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The model described here is settled — it is specified in
[`spec/data-model.md`](https://github.com/etabli-dev/etabli-recueil/blob/main/spec/data-model.md)
and drawn in [`spec/erd.mmd`](https://github.com/etabli-dev/etabli-recueil/blob/main/spec/erd.mmd) —
and it is implemented: documents, items, attachments, collections, tags, notes, annotations, custom
fields, the Office facet, the review queue and the provenance tables are all in the tree. The graph
and systematic-review tables are specified and not yet built.
:::

Four ideas carry most of the weight: the separation of **documents from items**, **content-hash
identity**, **facets**, and **provenance on every derived fact**. Get these four and the API, the
CLI and the plugin hooks all read as obvious consequences.

## Documents, items, attachments

Most reference managers conflate the file with the record about the file. Recueil does not, because
the two have different identities, different lifetimes and different sources of truth.

| Concept | What it is | Identity |
|---|---|---|
| **Document** | A file. A PDF, a scan, an email, a photo, a dataset archive. Bytes plus MIME type, size and the provenance of where it came from. | Its SHA-256 |
| **Item** | The library record. A thing you cite, file or read: an article, book, chapter, report, thesis, dataset, preprint, webpage, invoice, letter, contract, photo. | An internal id |
| **Attachment** | The relation between the two, carrying a role: `primary`, `supplement`, `snapshot`, `scan`. | The pair, plus its role |

The relation is genuinely many-to-many, and both directions occur in practice:

- **One item, many documents.** A paper with its published PDF, its accepted manuscript, its
  supplementary spreadsheet and an HTML snapshot of the landing page. Four documents, one item.
- **One document, many items.** A single conference proceedings PDF that is the primary attachment
  of nine chapter items. One document, stored once, nine items.

### Why the separation earns its keep

- The same bytes are stored once, no matter how many items point at them. Deduplication is a
  property of the model rather than a maintenance task.
- Re-downloading a paper you already have is a no-op that gets logged, not a second copy.
- An item can exist with no document at all — a book you have read but do not have a scan of, a
  reference found in someone else's bibliography — and gain one later without changing identity.
- A document can exist with no item, sitting in the review queue, waiting for a decision about what
  it actually is.

## Content-hash identity

**A file is its bytes.** The SHA-256 of a document's content is its identity. Path, filename and
modification time are metadata about a copy, never a statement about sameness
([ADR-0004](adr.qmd)).

This one decision resolves a surprising number of arguments:

- Ingesting the same file twice, from the scanner and again by email, links to the existing document
  and stops. The pipeline is idempotent by construction.
- Storage is content-addressed, so the layout on disk is derived from the hash and does not depend
  on the database. The store is readable and re-importable without the application, which is what
  "no lock-in" has to mean to be worth saying.
- Backups deduplicate well, and integrity checking is a rehash rather than a trust exercise.
- Rename anything you like. Nothing breaks.

### What the hash does not solve

Identical bytes prove sameness. **Different bytes prove nothing.** The same paper downloaded from
the publisher and from a repository differs by a watermark; a re-scan of the same page differs
everywhere. These are *near-duplicates*, and they are handled by a separate layer — a simhash over
extracted text — which **flags and never merges automatically**. Byte-identical files are linked
without asking; anything else goes to a human, with the reason recorded.

## Facets

An item's *type* says what it is. Its *facets* say which vocabularies apply to it. A facet is a
coherent block of fields attached to an item, rather than a hundred nullable columns that are empty
for most records.

| Facet | Fields | Applies to |
|---|---|---|
| **Bibliographic** | title, creators, venue, date, identifiers (DOI, PMID, PMCID, arXiv, ISBN, OpenAlex, S2), abstract, keywords, MeSH terms, language, citation key | Scholarly items |
| **Office** | correspondent, document date, archive serial number, amount, reference number | Private and office documents, mapping Paperless-ngx's model |

An item can carry both, and this is the point rather than an edge case. A standards document is
correspondence *and* something you cite. An invoice from a publisher is an office document that
belongs in a project collection. Facets let one library hold your reading and your filing without
either pretending to be the other, and without a scanned electricity bill acquiring an empty
"journal volume" field.

Beyond facets, arbitrary structure comes from **custom fields** — typed as text, number, date,
choice, multi-choice, JSON or item-reference. The same mechanism that adds a field to your invoices
is the mechanism that generates a systematic-review extraction form, which is why extraction data
comes out of the tool as a table rather than as a reshaping exercise.

## Provenance

**Every derived fact records where it came from.** Not the item — the *field*. Not the graph — the
*edge*.

A metadata field carries its source, the timestamp it was fetched, and a confidence. A graph edge
carries the same, plus its evidence, which for a citation extracted from a PDF is the sentence
around it. A merge carries the record of what was merged and stays reversible.

This buys four things:

1. **Merge policy that is not a guess.** When Crossref and OpenAlex disagree about a page range, the
   per-field source ordering decides, and the decision is inspectable afterwards.
2. **Manual edits that survive.** A field you have corrected by hand is locked and no resolver
   overwrites it. Enrichment can be re-run as often as you like without fear.
3. **Honest maps.** Every network view shows coverage statistics beside it: how many items had
   reference data, from which sources, fetched when. A co-citation map built on 40% coverage is a
   different object from one built on 95%, and the difference must be visible or the map is
   misleading.
4. **Reproducibility.** A frozen curated network embeds the metadata as it stood at freeze time, so
   a figure in a paper still means what it meant when it was made.

## Supporting concepts

| Concept | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Collection** | Hierarchical grouping, by hand. An item can be in several. |
| **Tag** | Flat label with a colour and a scheme. |
| **Note** | Markdown, attached to an item or standing alone. |
| **Annotation** | A highlight, note, area or ink mark on a document. Stored as a record against a target and a selector using the W3C Web Annotation model ([ADR-0009](adr.qmd), [ADR-0017](adr.qmd)), which is what makes it portable across every platform's PDF viewer and exportable back into an embedded PDF annotation. |
| **Creator** | A person, with name forms, ORCID and OpenAlex author id, and an explicit disambiguation status. |
| **Term** | A vocabulary entry in a scheme — author keyword, MeSH with its tree numbers, tag, OpenAlex topic, custom — with thesaurus mapping rules. This is the layer that makes co-word maps roll up sensibly instead of showing "COVID-19", "covid 19" and "SARS-CoV-2" as three nodes. |
| **ShadowWork** | An external work known only from a reference list or a deep dive. It participates in the graph, is never confused with something you own, and can be promoted to a real item. |
| **Review queue** | Where anything ambiguous goes, with its reason and a proposed action. |
| **Job** | A long-running operation with an idempotency key and a log. Imports, enrichment and dedup runs are resumable and safe to re-run. |
| **Audit log and trash** | Nothing is deleted. Deletion is a move to trash with restore, on top of an append-only audit log recording actor, action and before/after state. |

## The ten principles

The four ideas above are consequences of a shorter list. In full, from
[CONCEPT.md §3](https://github.com/etabli-dev/etabli-recueil/blob/main/CONCEPT.md):

1. The server is the source of truth.
2. Content hash is identity.
3. Flag, never guess.
4. Provenance on every derived fact.
5. Never delete.
6. API-first.
7. Reuse over rebuild.
8. Plugin contract before UI.
9. Idempotent, resumable batch operations.
10. No lock-in.
